title: Normal Operation
content:
P-101 is a process pump used to transfer material through the separation section.

During normal operation, operators should monitor pump status and available operating indicators.

title: Shift Handover
content: Any abnormal equipment indication observed during the shift should be included in the shift handover with the supporting event or equipment record.

title: Evidence Boundary
content: This document describes normal operating guidance. It does not determine the root cause of an equipment abnormality.

title: Vibration Monitoring
content:
P-101 vibration should be monitored when abnormal vibration is detected.

A high-vibration alarm is an indication requiring operator attention.

Repeated or increasing vibration should be reviewed by the appropriate maintenance or engineering personnel.

title: Shift Handover
content:
A high-vibration alarm should be reported in the shift handover when it occurs.

The handover should include:

- Equipment ID
- Alarm or observation
- Recorded vibration value when available
- Current equipment status
- Supporting evidence

title: Evidence Boundary
content: A vibration alarm alone does not establish the root cause of the vibration or confirm equipment damage.

title: Temperature Monitoring
content:
R-101 temperature should be monitored during operation.

A high-temperature alarm indicates an abnormal operating condition requiring attention.

title: Shift Handover
content:
When a high-temperature alarm occurs, the handover should record:

- Equipment ID
- Alarm condition
- Recorded temperature when available
- Current equipment status
- Supporting evidence

title: Evidence Boundary
content: A high-temperature alarm does not by itself establish the root cause of the condition or indicate equipment damage.

title: Handover Content
content:
A shift handover should communicate:

- Production status
- Important operational events
- Equipment issues
- Open maintenance actions
- Relevant observations
- Items requiring attention from the next shift

title: Evidence
content:
Operational statements should be supported by available records.

Reference documents may provide operating guidance but do not prove that an event occurred.

title: Human Review
content:
The generated handover is decision support.

The receiving operator or responsible human reviewer remains responsible for reviewing the information before acting on it.

title: Response
content:
When equipment protection trips:

1. Record the equipment identity.
2. Record the trip condition and available event information.
3. Confirm the current equipment status.
4. Follow the applicable approved recovery and inspection procedure.
5. Record open maintenance or inspection actions in the shift handover.

title: Important
content: The handover system must not authorize equipment restart or modify process parameters.

title: Evidence Boundary
content: A protection trip does not establish its root cause unless supporting evidence is available.

title: Response
content:
When a high-temperature alarm is observed:

1. Confirm the equipment identity and alarm condition.
2. Record the available temperature reading.
3. Monitor the equipment condition.
4. Follow the applicable approved operating procedure.
5. Record the event and relevant observations in the shift handover.

title: Important
content: The handover system must not independently change process parameters or issue equipment control commands.

title: Evidence Boundary
content: A high-temperature alarm does not establish a root cause unless supporting evidence is available.

title: Response
content:
When a high-vibration alarm is observed:

1. Confirm the equipment identity and alarm condition.
2. Record the available vibration reading.
3. Monitor the equipment condition.
4. Notify the appropriate maintenance or engineering role according to site practice.
5. Record the event and relevant observations in the shift handover.

title: Important
content: The procedure does not authorize the handover system to directly control or change equipment operating parameters.

title: Evidence Boundary
content: The procedure provides response guidance. It does not establish the cause of an individual equipment event.
